textbookText: 31. A complex number is generally expressed in the form: A) a + ib, where a and b are real numbers and i = √−1 B) a + b, with no imaginary component C) a × ib only, without addition D) i alone, without any real part
32. The value of i² is: A) −1 B) 1 C) i D) −i
33. The value of i⁴ is: A) 1 B) −1 C) i D) 0
34. The conjugate of the complex number z = a + ib is: A) a − ib B) −a + ib C) −a − ib D) b + ia
35. The modulus (absolute value) of z = a + ib is given by: A) √(a² + b²) B) a² + b² C) a + b D) √(a − b)

36. The product of a complex number and its conjugate, z × z̄, equals: A) a² + b², which is always a real, non-negative number B) 2a (real part doubled) C) 2ib (imaginary part doubled) D) A complex number with non-zero imaginary part

37. The argument (amplitude) of a complex number z = a + ib is defined as: A) θ = tan⁻¹(b/a), the angle made with the positive real axis B) θ = a/b directly, without any trigonometric function C) θ = √(a² + b²) D) θ = a + b
38. The polar form of a complex number z = a + ib is written as: A) z = r(cos θ + i sin θ), where r is the modulus and θ the argument B) z = r × θ C) z = a × b(cos θ) D) z = r² (cos θ + i sin θ)
39. Which of the following is an example of a purely imaginary number? A) 5i (real part = 0) B) 5 + 0i C) 0 + 0i D) 5 − 5i
40. According to De Moivre's theorem, (cos θ + i sin θ)ⁿ equals: A) cos(nθ) + i sin(nθ) B) n(cos θ + i sin θ) C) cos θⁿ + i sin θⁿ, meaning θ raised to the power n D) cos(θ/n) + i sin(θ/n)
41. The sum of a complex number and its conjugate, z + z̄, is always: A) A real number, equal to 2a (twice the real part) B) A purely imaginary number C) Always zero D) Equal to the modulus of z

42. Which of the following extraordinary facts about complex numbers is TRUE? A) Complex numbers, despite containing √−1, are essential in real engineering fields like electrical AC circuit analysis and quantum mechanics B) Complex numbers have no real-world applications, existing only in pure theory C) Complex numbers cannot be multiplied or divided, only added D) Every complex number is actually a real number in disguise

43. In the Argand plane (complex plane), the horizontal axis represents: A) The real part of the complex number B) The imaginary part of the complex number C) The modulus of the complex number D) The argument of the complex number
44. The multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of a non-zero complex number z = a + ib is: A) z̄ / |z|² = (a − ib)/(a² + b²) B) z itself C) −z D) |z|² / z̄
45. Which of the following equations has complex (non-real) roots? A) x² + 1 = 0 B) x² − 1 = 0 C) x² − 4 = 0 D) x² − 9 = 0

46. When multiplying two complex numbers in polar form, r₁(cosθ₁+isinθ₁) and r₂(cosθ₂+isinθ₂), the result has: A) Modulus r₁r₂ and argument (θ₁+θ₂) B) Modulus r₁+r₂ and argument θ₁θ₂ C) Modulus r₁r₂ and argument (θ₁−θ₂) D) Modulus r₁/r₂ and argument (θ₁+θ₂)
47. The cube roots of unity (solutions of x³ = 1) are: A) 1, ω, ω², where ω = (−1+i√3)/2 is a complex cube root of unity B) 1, −1, i only C) 1, 2, 3 D) Only the real number 1, with no complex roots
48. The sum of the three cube roots of unity (1 + ω + ω²) equals: A) 0 B) 1 C) 3 D) −1

49. Geometrically, multiplying a complex number by i corresponds to: A) Rotating the point representing the complex number by 90° counterclockwise about the origin in the Argand plane B) Reflecting the point across the real axis C) Doubling the modulus of the complex number D) No change in position at all
50. The quadratic formula applied to ax² + bx + c = 0 gives complex roots when: A) The discriminant (b² − 4ac) is negative B) The discriminant is positive C) The discriminant equals zero D) a = 0

51. Which of the following is TRUE regarding equality of two complex numbers a + ib and c + id? A) They are equal if and only if a = c and b = d (real and imaginary parts separately equal) B) They are equal whenever their moduli are equal, regardless of argument C) They can never be equal unless both are zero D) They are equal if a + b = c + d
52. |z₁z₂| (modulus of the product of two complex numbers) equals: A) |z₁| × |z₂| B) |z₁| + |z₂| C) |z₁|² × |z₂|² D) |z₁ + z₂|

53. Historically, complex numbers were first seriously considered by mathematicians while solving: A) Cubic equations, where intermediate steps required square roots of negative numbers even for real solutions B) Simple linear equations only C) Basic addition and subtraction problems D) Problems involving only positive integers
54. The imaginary unit i is defined such that: A) i = √−1, so i² = −1 B) i = −1 directly, without any square root C) i is a real number equal to 1 D) i has no defined value in mathematics
55. If z = 3 + 4i, then |z| equals: A) 5 B) 7 C) 25 D) 1
